subject: DPA clarifications — controller/processor roles, subprocessors, breach notice

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: DPA clarifications & next steps

Hi Susan — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on the privacy items that came up: 

- Controller vs. Processor: you asked us to confirm the role Redwood will take in the relationship.
- Subprocessors: you wanted a list of downstream subprocessors and a mechanism for updates.
- Breach notice / incident timeline: clarify our notification SLA and escalation playbook.
- Data residency & retention: confirm default logging retention and options for EEA-only storage.
- PII handling & training: confirm whether customer content is used for model training and what opt-outs exist.

Can you send over Harbor Bank's security questionnaire (if you have one) and highlight any firm non-starters? I can loop in our legal lead (Marissa) for any redlines once we have your DPA points.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share the questionnaire / call out the must-haves (by Mon 7/12)
2) We return a redlined DPA and answers to the questions (by Wed 7/14)
3) Align on any residency addendum or subprocessors list and sign via DocuSign.

Attaching the short call notes. Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183

From: Susan Jenkins <susan.jenkins@harborbank.com>

Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@harborbank.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: DPA clarifications & next steps

Ben — thanks for the recap. Attaching our security questionnaire (HarborBank_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx). Couple of clarifications up front: 

1) Controller/Processor: Our procurement team requires a contractual confirmation that Harbor Bank is the Controller and Redwood is the Processor. Is that your standard position?
2) Subprocessors: We need a current list of subprocessors and at least 30 days notice for any changes; any common cloud providers are fine but we need names and contact details.
3) Breach notice: Harbor's policy requires notification "without undue delay" and detailed incident reporting within 72 hours for incidents affecting PII. Will you commit to that timeline?
4) Data residency: For our US retail banking data we require data to remain in US regions; do you have an EEA residency addendum if we expand there?
5) Training & use: Please confirm whether Redwood uses customer content to improve models or training unless explicitly opted out.

We highlighted a few mandatory controls in the questionnaire — see tabs 2/3. If you can provide the redline and answers by Wed that would be ideal; otherwise let us know if you need more time.

Thanks,
Susan
Director, Procurement — Harbor Bank
susan.jenkins@harborbank.com

Attachments: HarborBank_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx

Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 14:27:48 -0700
Subject: DPA redline + answers to questions (draft)

Susan — thanks for the questionnaire. See attached a redlined DPA (DPA_Redline_v2.pdf) that reflects our standard positions and initial responses to the checklist items. High-level answers below; Marissa (cc'd) from Legal will confirm the contractual language.

- Controller/Processor: Redwood's standard contract treats the customer as Controller and Redwood as Processor. We can confirm that in the DPA.
- Subprocessors: our current subprocessors include: AWS (us-west-2), GCP (us-central1) for optional deployments, Sentry (monitoring), Datadog (optional telemetry), and Stripe (billing). We maintain a public subprocessors list and provide 30 days' notice for material changes.
- Breach notification: our policy is to notify affected customers within 72 hours of discovery for incidents involving customer data and provide regular updates until resolution. For critical incidents we will notify ASAP and follow up with a full incident report.
- Data residency: we support region pinning for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers default to US regions. We can discuss an EEA addendum if you plan EU processing.
- Training & use: Redwood does not use customer-provided content to train models unless you opt in via contract. By default, customer content is not used for model training.

Links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/9831
- If these terms look good we can send a DocuSign for signature; draft DocuSign link included in the final packet.

Attaching: DPA_Redline_v2.pdf

Ben
Account Executive
--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Jenkins <susan.jenkins@harborbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: DPA clarifications — controller/processor roles, subprocessors, breach notice

Hi Susan — looping in Legal to answer formally. Below are the items we can confirm today; the attached DPA redline includes the matching contract language. If anything below is a blocker please flag and we'll prioritize.

1) Roles (Controller/Processor)
- Confirmed: Harbor Bank is Controller; Redwood Inference is Processor. This language is in the DPA (see Section 1.1).

2) Subprocessors
- Current subprocessors (as of 2027-07-15):
  - AWS (Amazon Web Services) — hosting (us-west-2)
  - Google Cloud Platform — optional deployments (us-central1)
  - Sentry — error monitoring
  - Datadog — telemetry (optional)
  - Stripe — billing
- We publish a public subprocessors list and will provide at least 30 days' notice for material changes. If Harbor requires contractually mandated approval for a specific subprocessor we can add a clause to the DPA (may require limited exceptions).

3) Breach notification & incident handling
- We commit to notifying Harbor without undue delay and provide an initial notification within 72 hours of becoming aware of an incident affecting customer data. For critical incidents we'll send immediate alerts and follow-up with a full incident report and remediation plan. This is reflected in Section 5 of the redline.

4) Logging & retention
- Default: application logs and request metadata are retained for 90 days for hosted customers.
- Dedicated/Private: we can configure retention windows to meet Harbor's policy (longer retention possible under a config/addendum).
- Audit logs (security/audit events) retention can be extended via an add-on.

5) Data residency & region pinning
- Hosted accounts default to US regions; Dedicated and Private deployments support region pinning for US-only or EEA-only storage. We can provide an EEA residency addendum if you expect EU processing.

6) PII & model training
- By default Redwood does not use customer-provided content to train models. Any use for model improvement requires explicit opt-in (contractual).

Next steps: 
- Please review the attached DPA_Redline_v2.pdf and the redline comments. If the DPA looks acceptable we can proceed to DocuSign and aim to finalize this week.
- If Harbor needs a formal EEA residency addendum or a custom subprocessor approval clause, let us know and we will route to Legal/Engineering for impact and timing.

If helpful I can set a 30-minute call with our security lead to walk through the questionnaire items you flagged.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0124

Attachments: DPA_Redline_v2.pdf
